notes: Every assertion passed in both configurations (22/22 each). The assertions are non-discriminating on this model for everyday screens: plain Claude already avoids emoji icons, purple gradients, missing labels and mobile overflow on these prompts.

The with-skill runs all rendered their pages (headless Chrome at desktop, tablet and phone widths, plus dark mode and error/empty states) and fixed problems they found: a misaligned logo, stretched buttons, a broken sticky table header, mobile filter overflow and a pagination bar showing under the empty state. No baseline run rendered its output.
Cost: the with-skill runs took about 3.8x longer (316s vs 83s on average) and used about 1.8x the tokens (111k vs 61k), mostly spent on the screenshot-and-fix loop.

Next iteration: add prompts that need expressive, award-level design and motion (scroll storytelling, kinetic type, pinned sections), where the gap between default and skilled output is larger, plus assertions on reduced-motion support and animation performance.
